clue.text: Word describing acid hermit, no saint

indicators.note: no tells us to drop the saint from the hermit word, leaving it short by a letter

parts.note: an ascetic is a self-denying recluse, like a hermit

explanation.surface: A hermit who is no saint is described in somewhat chemical terms.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetic acid is the acid in vinegar, so the adjective is literally a word used to describe an acid.

clue.text: Mark called around to entertain this writer

indicators.note: to entertain means to hold a guest, so one piece is taken inside the other
around suggests the letters of called are moved about into a new order

parts.note: the setter referring to themself, giving I

explanation.surface: Someone describes a mark they phoned about while hosting the writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' rearranges CALLED into CEDLLA; 'to entertain' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cedilla is the small hook mark placed under a c, as in façade, so it is a diacritical mark.

clue.text: Walk quietly, following vehicle

indicators.note: following places the quiet letter after the vehicle in the answer

parts.note: a tram is a vehicle running on rails
P stands for piano, the musical direction to play quietly

explanation.surface: Someone walks softly behind a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: To tramp is to walk heavily or trudge a long way, a synonym for walk.

clue.text: Firm and politician within the law or sharing guilt?

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
MP is a Member of Parliament
licit means lawful, permitted by law

explanation.surface: A company and a politician both act lawfully, or perhaps they are partners in wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone complicit is involved with others in wrongdoing, so they share the guilt.

clue.text: Duty has changed with king being guarded for 24 hours

indicators.note: being guarded means held inside, so the king's letter sits within the other letters
changed tells us the letters of duty has are put in a new order

parts.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A duty roster changes so that the king is protected around the clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' turns DUTY HAS into THUSDAY; 'being guarded' puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Thursday is one particular day, a single period of twenty-four hours.

clue.text: Worker with little power in time is becoming so much the worse

indicators.note: in places the worker and the power letter inside the time and is letters

parts.note: the ant is the crossword's usual worker insect
P is the abbreviation for power, little meaning abbreviated

explanation.surface: An underpowered worker gets worse as time passes.
explanation.walkthrough: TANT PIS is a French phrase used in English.
explanation.definitionFit: The French expression tant pis means too bad or never mind, literally so much the worse.

clue.text: At university group creates disorder

parts.note: being up means being in residence at university, especially Oxford or Cambridge
a set is a group or clique

explanation.surface: A student group causes chaos on campus.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage you are 'up' at university when in residence there.
explanation.definitionFit: An upset is a disturbance or disorder, as in a stomach upset.

clue.text: Don's cruel, wicked, nasty bit of work

indicators.note: wicked suggests the letters are twisted out of their order

parts.note: the letters of the name with its s

explanation.surface: A man called Don is cruel and wicked, a thoroughly nasty piece of work.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoundrel is a villain or rogue, a person described as a nasty bit of work.

clue.text: Element that would be disastrous for skin care (not potassium)

indicators.note: disastrous suggests the letters are thrown into chaos and rearranged
not tells us the potassium letter is taken away from skin care

parts.note: K is the chemical symbol for potassium

explanation.surface: A toxic element would be a terrible thing to put in a skincare product.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes K from SKINCARE, leaving SINCARE; 'disastrous' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenic is a chemical element, number 33, famous as a poison.

clue.text: Oxford types eventually giving opportunities to ambitious youngsters?

definitions.text: Oxford types eventually giving opportunities to ambitious youngsters?

parts.words: Oxford types eventually giving opportunities to ambitious youngsters?
parts.note: Oxfords are a style of shoe; once their wearers die, their jobs fall to younger people

explanation.walkthrough: 'Oxford types' suggests university people, but Oxfords are lace-up shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes positions that only open up when the present holder dies or retires.

clue.text: Not suitable footwear for office? There may be reversal of policy

definitions.meaning: a rubber thong sandal is too casual for wearing at work

definitions.text: There may be reversal of policy
definitions.meaning: a sudden U-turn by a politician

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a casual thong sandal and an abrupt change of political stance.

clue.text: Article in temporary accommodation? One isn't in one's own home

definitions.text: One isn't in one's own home

indicators.note: in places the article inside the temporary accommodation

parts.note: a tent is a temporary shelter
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone lodging in a tent is not living in a home of their own.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenant rents a home owned by someone else, so they do not live in property of their own.

clue.text: Sailor with raincoat that may get run over by car

definitions.text: that may get run over by car

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
mac is short for mackintosh, a British raincoat

explanation.surface: A sailor in a raincoat risks being knocked down by a car.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarmac is the road surfacing material that cars drive over.

clue.text: Foreign noblemen are cemetery vandals maybe!

definitions.meaning: German princes or counts ruling border territories
split three and five, the word says what vandals do to tombs: damage burial plots

explanation.definitionFit: Margraves were hereditary German noblemen in charge of border provinces.

clue.text: Take away area for vehicle to reverse on

indicators.note: to reverse tells us the vehicle word is read backwards

parts.note: a bus is a vehicle
a tract is an area of land

explanation.surface: A stretch of land is set aside for vehicles to back up on.
explanation.definitionFit: To subtract is to take one number away from another.

clue.text: Reverse decision to sponsor part of athletics stadium

parts.note: to back someone is to support or sponsor them
the running track circles an athletics stadium

explanation.surface: A decision to fund a section of a sports stadium is reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: To backtrack is to retreat from a previous position or decision.

clue.text: Grumble, needing to remove a roguish head of state

indicators.note: needing to remove says the letter a is taken out of the grumble word

parts.note: to moan is to grumble
arch means playfully mischievous or roguish

explanation.surface: A complaint about getting rid of a mischievous ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing to remove a' drops A from MOAN, leaving MON.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch, a king or queen, is a head of state.

clue.text: It's liable to be a part of the curriculum

definitions.meaning: an adjective meaning likely to be affected, as in prone to delays
a school course such as history or maths

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means liable or prone; as a noun, a field of study taught at school.

clue.text: Religious leader, one installed in new chapel not English

indicators.note: installed in means placed inside, so the one is set within the other letters
new says the letters of chapel are made into a fresh arrangement
not tells us the English letter is taken out of chapel

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A religious leader is appointed to a newly built chapel that is not English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' drops E from CHAPEL, leaving CHAPL; 'new' rearranges it to CALPH; 'installed in' puts I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A caliph was the chief Muslim ruler, successor to the Prophet, a religious leader.

clue.text: Religious act of writer joining an established church

parts.note: a pen is a writing tool
CE is the Church of England, the established church in England

explanation.surface: A writer joins the Church of England as an act of faith.
explanation.definitionFit: Penance is a religious act of contrition performed to atone for sin.

clue.text: What may give some partners no rest

definitions.text: What may give some partners no rest

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something keeps people's partners awake at night.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'What may' cannot stand for the answer; the whole clue defines it while 'some' hides it, a semi-all-in-one.
explanation.definitionFit: Loud nocturnal breathing noises keep a bed partner awake.

clue.text: Merry frolic of runner in Berlin

definitions.meaning: a lively bout of fun or indulgence
the river flowing through Berlin; runner is crossword slang for river

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a lively bout of fun and is also the river through Berlin.

clue.text: Some birds showed aggression to others

parts.note: bit means attacked with the teeth or beak
terns are other birds, seabirds besides the ones defined

explanation.surface: Some birds attacked their neighbours.
explanation.walkthrough: Split three and five, the answer says the birds bit some terns.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitterns are wading birds of the heron family.

clue.text: Priest coming down on the heartless people of superior status

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming down on means sitting above the next piece

parts.note: Eli is the priest in the Bible who raised Samuel

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of the word is removed

explanation.surface: A priest descends upon the heartless.
explanation.definitionFit: The elite are a select group regarded as superior in status.

clue.text: Repeated noise from ranter, bore I've beaten up!

indicators.note: beaten up suggests the letters are knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone complains about the noise from a ranting, boring person who has been assaulted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beaten up' rearranges RANTER, BORE and IVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A reverberation is a sound that echoes, repeating itself.

clue.text: Most pure little man facing trial

indicators.note: facing puts the man in front of the trial in the answer

parts.note: Chas is a short form of the man's name Charles
a test is a trial

explanation.surface: A small man faces a trial.
explanation.definitionFit: Chastest is the superlative of chaste, meaning pure or virtuous.

clue.text: Sportsperson's message against making UK republic

definitions.meaning: a goalkeeper in football or wicketkeeper in cricket
split four and two, it reads as a monarchist slogan to retain ER, the Queen

explanation.walkthrough: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A keeper is a goalkeeper or wicketkeeper; as a phrase it urges retaining the monarch.
